title: What If China Nuked Guam With One DF-26?
description:
What would a Chinese nuclear missile do to Guam, and how many minutes would anyone have?

In our simulation a DF-26 launched from southern China reaches Guam in about 13 minutes, and the video shows the flight clock first, then the blast rings of a 10 kiloton airburst over Andersen Air Force Base.

One forty-three in the morning on Guam: a nuclear weapon bursts over Andersen Air Force Base. Thirteen minutes earlier, a launcher in southern China raised a DF-26 missile and fired. Six other missiles are already in the air toward Kadena, Yokosuka and Naval Base Guam, and only one of the seven is nuclear. By the end of that first hour, how many American fighters in the western Pacific can still take off?

This is a simulation. It has not happened. Scenario segments are labelled SIMULATION on screen; facts are labelled REAL DATA or REAL HISTORY. The launch sites, targets, the single nuclear warhead and its 10 kiloton yield are our choices, a scenario, not a forecast and not a known Chinese plan, and we set no date. China's declared policy is no first use.

How this video was made: the narration is AI-generated (Google Text-to-Speech). Scenario segments are simulations built from published models and open sources; the launch sites, warhead, yield, targets and timing are ours.
Maps: Natural Earth (public domain), OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) via OpenFreeMap and OpenMapTiles. Thumbnail backgrounds are AI-generated. Music: generated with Eleven Music.
